facts.statement: Rexarthuria lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Valanginian age.
The type locality for Rexarthuria is the Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Rexarthuria were found in the upper Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation in England.
facts.quote: found in the early Cretaceous (Valanginian age) of the upper Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation in England

facts.statement: Rexarthuria is a newly proposed genus and a new combination.
The only known species in the genus Rexarthuria is Rexarthuria cliftii.
The species was originally placed in the genus Palaeornis, but that name was preoccupied by a bird.
facts.quote: originally placed in the genus Palaeornis, which is preoccupied by a bird

facts.statement: The specific name 'cliftii' honors William Clift, who was the curator of the Hunterian Museum.
facts.quote: The specific name honours William Clift, the curator of the Hunterian Museum

facts.statement: In 2009, Witton and colleagues re-examined the specimen and classified it as a lonchodectid rather than an ornithocheirid.
facts.quote: Mark P. Witton et al. (2009) re-examined the type specimen and realized that "P." clifti is not an ornithocheirid, referring it to Lonchodectidae based on similarities to humeri assigned to Lonchodectes by Hooley (1914)

facts.statement: In 2025, Thomas and McDavid analyzed the taxon as a sister group to Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: In 2025, Thomas and McDavid recovered it as a sister taxon of Tapejaridae

facts.statement: Averianov referred the taxon to indeterminate Azhdarchoidea in his 2012 and 2014 assessments.
facts.quote: Averianov (2012, 2014) referred the taxon to Azhdarchoidea indeterminate in his re-assessment of Ornithostoma

rejected.statement: Rexarthuria is an extinct genus of azhdarchoid pterosaur known only from fragments of a single humerus.
rejected.quote: Rexarthuria is an extinct genus of azhdarchoid pterosaur known from parts of a single humerus (upper arm bone)
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Rexarthuria is an extinct genus of azhdarchoid pterosaur'

rejected.statement: The genus Rexarthuria was described by Thomas and McDavid in 2026.
